## My thinking this year — start of the season

I've been working these 8 mu for 20 years now. At 65, I'm not going to experiment with anything wild — but I've read the extension materials, I went to some training sessions back when my son was in school, and I understand my soil pretty well by now. This plot is loamy, decent organic matter because I've been returning straw for years. It's productive ground if I manage it properly.

Ten people in the household sounds like a lot, but really only two or three are steady help on the farm — my wife, myself, and my younger son when he's between construction jobs. The others are off-farm, in school, or too young. So for 8 mu I can handle the fieldwork, but I still hire the combine for wheat harvest and the corn picker for maize — no sense buying machinery for this much land.

### Wheat (October to June, 8 mu)

I plant in mid-October, around the 10th to 15th — the old saying is "寒露种麦正当时" and our area fits that. I use a local improved variety, something like Jimai 22 or Shiluan 02-1, whatever the agricultural supply shop has this year that's been reliable. I usually save a bit of seed from my own clean plot but mostly buy fresh every 2-3 years.

For fertilizer, I target about **16 kg N/mu total** — that's on the modest side, but with straw return my soil holds nitrogen well and I don't want to waste money or push too hard. I apply 45% compound (15-15-15) at about 40 kg/mu as basal before planting — that gives me the phosphorus and potassium I need plus some starter N. Then at jointing (late March), if the crop color is right I topdress 15-18 kg of urea/mu. If it looks pale I'll push to 20. This is a split approach, because applying it all at planting wastes nitrogen to leaching over winter — I learned that from the extension engineer maybe fifteen years ago and I've always split since then.

Irrigation — this is where costs add up. Our well is metered now, costs about 35 yuan per mu per watering. I plan 4 irrigations: one before winter (around late November, to insure against dry winter), jointing in late March, heading in late April, and grain-filling mid-May. If spring rain is good I might skip heading or cut back. Four times is standard here; some neighbors do 5, but I find 4 is enough on my soil.

Herbicide once in spring (broadleaf mix, maybe chlortoluron for grass weeds). Aphids in May if I see them — one spray of imidacloprid usually handles it. I watch for stripe rust because it hit us hard in 2019, but I only spray fungicide if I see symptoms.

Yield target: about **470 kg/mu**. I got 490 last year, 450 the year before — it depends heavily on the May weather (hot dry wind at grain fill is what kills us).

### Maize (June to September, 8 mu)

Right after wheat harvest — the combine finishes around June 10, and I want maize in the ground within a week. I use no-till direct seeding, hire the planter (a neighbor has one, charges 50 yuan/mu). Straw is chopped and left on the surface, which keeps moisture in during the hot June. Variety is a hybrid, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335 or whatever's moving at the shop — I like 958 for this soil.

Fertilizer: one application is what most of us do now, a compound bulk-blend at roughly **15 kg N/mu, 5 kg P, 5 kg K**, banded near the seed or spread and incorporated. I used to split but with the summer heat and single fill-up planters now I just do it once at the big flare stage (V6-V8, about 30 days after emergence). That's enough — the rainy season carries it.

Irrigation: usually only need 1-2 times. June if it's dry for emergence, and tasseling (late July/early August) if the rains haven't come. Our summer is the rainy season so usually maize doesn't need much from the well.

Herbicide post-emergence (atrazine + nicosulfuron mix, standard). Corn borer I handle with granular insecticide at whorl stage — we have a lot of borer pressure in this area.

Yield target: **520 kg/mu**. Last year I got 540, which was a good year.

### Cost and labor thinking

Input costs (seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation water) come to roughly **5,400 yuan for the full year** across both crops. Add custom machinery services (harvest, planting) and it's closer to 8,000. Our gross from both crops is usually 15,000-17,000 yuan, so margin is tight — this is why 8 mu alone can't support a family, and my sons work off-farm. I'm not chasing maximum yield, I'm chasing reliable yield with controlled costs.
